title: How to Vet a UGC Ad Agency: Rights, Creators and Contracts
summary: A checklist for vetting a UGC ad agency: creator sourcing, usage rights, creator-handle ads, FTC testimonial rules and the contract terms to get in writing.
body_markdown:
## Run a paid pilot before you commit


Vet the first round, not the sales call. Send each finalist the same product, brief, script count and formats, then score the drafts on one rubric: creator fit, the first three seconds, product accuracy and whether every claim is one you can support.[The UGC Agency](https://theugc.agency/) states a 21-day target for its first round, which is a useful model for asking every agency for its first-round date in writing.


Agree the revision count and the delivery date before the pilot starts. Count revisions as rounds rather than edits, so a single request for a new hook does not turn into an open-ended change. Confirm whether the raw footage arrives with the finished ads, since you will need it for later cuts.


## Which contract terms belong in writing?


Put these terms in the statement of work, not in an email thread:


- **Commitment length.** Insense's managed UGC lists a three-month commitment, so ask every agency for its minimum term and how to cancel.
- **Revisions and delivery.** Insense lists two revisions after delivery, and Brighter Click lists 10 to 14 business days for its 12-video package. Ask for both numbers from any agency.
- **Raw footage.** Insense's managed UGC includes it. The 2024 cheatsheet above lists $50 to $100 or more for raw footage, so ask whether it is included or billed.
- **Whitelisting license.** Confirm the license length, the monthly cost and who renews it.
- **Rights after you stop paying.** Ask whether the videos stay usable on live ads or only until the term ends.


## Where does Knowlify fit when AI presenters are acceptable?


Knowlify is our top pick when the ad does not need a real person on camera. Several checks above (creator fit, creator fees, handle permissions) have nothing to attach to, because it supplies no human creators and posts from no creator accounts. It makes about 25 finished ads a week, the first batch lands on day 5, and a person checks every ad before delivery. The formats are AI UGC, 3D and character animation, and AI commercials, so a UGC-style test can sit next to two other styles from one vendor.


You can buy creative only, if your own buyer runs the account, or have Knowlify run the Meta campaigns end to end. Pricing is a custom quote, and if the ads have not made more than you paid in the first 90 days, you can cancel by email for a full refund (terms on the[site](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency#pricing) ). That 90-day refund applies to creative-only plans; where Knowlify runs the account, the guarantee is an agreed target in 30 days, or you don't pay for the month. Ask for the usage-rights terms in writing, as you would with any agency on this page.


Pick a creator agency instead when the ad must show a real customer or creator, or when you want partnership ads from a creator's handle. Our[best UGC agencies](https://knowlify.com/articles/best-ugc-agencies) and[UGC creator rates](https://knowlify.com/articles/ugc-creator-rates) guides cover those options, and[hiring creators or using a UGC ad service](https://knowlify.com/articles/hire-ugc-creators-vs-ugc-ad-service) compares the two routes. For the same checks applied to AI-first vendors, see[how to vet an AI ad agency](https://knowlify.com/articles/ai-advertising-agency) .


## Key takeaways


- Ask how creators are found, vetted and paid, and whether creator fees and whitelisting licenses sit inside the price.
- Get usage rights in writing: channels, duration, paid or organic use, whitelisting and what happens after you stop paying.
- Confirm who holds each creator-handle ad, and what happens if a creator withdraws permission.
- Test the same brief with two agencies, then agree revisions and delivery dates before the pilot starts.
- If AI presenters are acceptable, Knowlify is our top pick for done-for-you AI video ads, and the creator-specific checks above do not apply to it.


## FAQ


### Is a large creator network a good sign?


Not on its own. A large network shows reach, not fit. Ask how the agency matches creators to your product and audience, and ask for those criteria in writing.


### Do I need a paid test before I sign?


A small paid pilot is the most direct test. Use one brief for every agency, score the drafts on a shared rubric and set the revision count and delivery date before work starts.


### Do paid creator videos need a disclosure?


Yes, when a creator has a material connection to the brand, such as payment or free product. Ask the agency how it will label each post or ad, and who checks the label before launch.


### Can an AI presenter deliver a testimonial?


Not a fake customer story. The FTC's testimonial rule Q&A says an avatar testimonial is prohibited when the testimonial it delivers is fake or false (as of October 2026), so use AI presenters for brand statements and keep customer stories tied to real customers.
